repro: repro/sec/zz-hunt-sec-push.test.ts (cp to convex/, npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-sec-push.test.ts; test 'SE-1')
notes: Attacker: any account, lowest privilege. Gain: blind POSTs from Convex's network to arbitrary https hosts (redirects are refused, the response body is never read), a weak status oracle, a signed VAPID token for an origin of their choice (not replayable to real push services because aud is bound), and a way to slow other members' urgent pushes. Impact is limited by https-only and by Convex's hosted runtime, hence Medium not High. Tester 6 owns the push cryptography; this is the URL handling only.
title: Any signed-in member (read-only included) can make the server POST to any https URL by naming it as a push endpoint (server-side request forgery).
steps: 1. Sign in as any member, e.g. a read-only one. 2. Call pushSubscriptions.subscribe with endpoint https://127.0.0.1:8443/admin (or https://169.254.169.254/..., https://[::1]:3210/..., https://10.0.0.5/..., or an attacker's own host) and any 87/22-character base64url keys; up to 10 endpoints per account. 3. Wait for, or cause, an urgent alert the member can see (a read-only member sees an overdue inspection). 4. convex/push.ts sendUrgent fetches each stored endpoint.
expected: Only real push services are accepted (fcm.googleapis.com, updates.push.services.mozilla.com, web.push.apple.com, *.notify.windows.com), or at least loopback, link-local and private addresses and bare IPs are refused, at subscribe time and again before the fetch.
actual: All five endpoints are stored and the Node action POSTs to each with the deployment's VAPID Authorization header (a JWT signed for aud=<that origin>, valid 12 h) and a body encrypted to keys the caller chose. A 404/410 answer deletes the row, which the caller can observe (the 10-device limit frees a slot), so answers of internal https services are distinguishable. Each endpoint may hold the sender for 15 s (PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS) and jobs run one after another, so one member with 10 slow endpoints delays every later member's push by up to 150 s per check.
evidence: repro/sec/zz-hunt-sec-push.test.ts output: 'SE-1 accepted endpoints' and 'SE-1 server fetched' list all five URLs. src/domain/pushSubscription.ts:31-35 (only checks https:// prefix), convex/push.ts:104-111 (fetch of device.endpoint), convex/webPushProtocol.ts:86 (VAPID token minted for whatever origin the endpoint names). Both earlier reviews state 'Outbound calls go to fixed https hosts'; this is the first caller-chosen URL.

notes: What leaks: the lock-screen card '<program name>: N urgent alerts' with alert titles (tail numbers, 'grounded', overdue inspections, expired dates) to whoever holds the device. Second effect is a safety-notification gap: B believes this device alerts them and it does not. Related known items S10/S6 are about stored data, not push. The UI half was proven by code reading only (headless Chromium has no push service).
title: A device keeps receiving an account's urgent-alert push messages after that account signs out, or after an administrator resets its password; nothing but disabling the account stops them, and the next person on the device sees the switch as on.
steps: 1. On a shared hangar tablet, member A turns on Settings > This device > Alert this device. 2. A signs out (or: A's phone is lost and an administrator resets A's password, which ends every session). 3. An urgent alert arises in A's program. 4. Server: convex/push.ts still sends to the device. 5. Member B signs in on the same tablet and opens Settings: the switch already shows ON (DeviceAlerts.tsx:86 sets it from the browser's subscription alone), so B never subscribes; the device goes on showing A's program alerts, not B's.
expected: Sign-out removes the device's subscription (the code comment says 'a device alerts whoever is signed in on it' and ADR-0012 line 23 says 'Signing in as someone else on the same device moves the subscription to that account'). A password reset, which the accounts runbook describes as cutting off every device, also ends push to those devices, or the member/administrator can see and remove devices. The switch reflects whether THIS account is subscribed.
actual: After auth:signOut the pushSubscriptions row remains and sendImmediate/sendUrgent still deliver ('SE-2 after sign-out: { pushed: 1, requests: 1, rows: 1 }'). Nothing in src/ calls unsubscribePush except the manual switch (grep: only DeviceAlerts.tsx:101 via pushDevice.ts:106); signOutLocal (src/data/store.ts:513) and signOutOfLive (src/main.tsx:283) do not. convex/admin.ts resetPassword/invalidateSessions and the disable path never touch pushSubscriptions (grep: the table is referenced only in pushSubscriptions.ts, push.ts, urgentAlerts.ts). There is no query listing a member's devices and unsubscribe needs the secret endpoint URL, so a lost device cannot be cut off remotely except by disabling the account. Nothing moves the row on sign-in either, contradicting ADR-0012.
evidence: repro/sec/zz-hunt-sec-push.test.ts test 'SE-2'; convex/pushSubscriptions.ts:52-60,87-97; src/components/DeviceAlerts.tsx:80-88; src/data/pushDevice.ts:102-108; src/main.tsx:283-289; docs/adr/0012-urgent-alerts-by-web-push-and-immediate-email.md:23; docs/runbooks/accounts.md:46.
suspect: src/main.tsx:283 (no unsubscribe on sign-out); src/components/DeviceAlerts.tsx:86; convex/admin.ts:258

repro: repro/sec/zz-hunt-sec-emailcap.test.ts (cp to convex/, npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-sec-emailcap.test.ts)
notes: Same family as the accepted T8 (shared FAA/Geoapify caps) but new since 4 Nov and it suppresses safety notifications rather than a lookup. It also happens honestly: 6 opted-in members x 10 urgent events in one program is 60. Device push is not capped, so members with 'Alert this device' on still hear at once. Also any member may opt in to urgent emails for themselves (setUrgentEmailPreference), which raises the per-event cost.
title: One Flight Program's administrator can spend the deployment-wide daily cap of 60 immediate urgent-alert emails in a minute, so every other program's 'aircraft grounded' and 'inspection overdue' emails silently wait for the next daily digest.
steps: 1. Sign in as the administrator of program B (any one program is enough). 2. Settings > Flight Program > Expiring dates: save a date already in the past. 3. Edit its date to another past day and save; repeat 60 times (each save is a new alert key 'date-expired|uuid|expiresOn', so each sends the administrator one immediate email and consumes one of IMMEDIATE_EMAILS_PER_DAY). No rate limit applies to expiringItems.save. 4. In program A a pilot reports a grounding problem.
expected: Program A's opted-in members get the immediate email. One program (or one user) cannot use the whole day's allowance: a per-program or per-recipient share, or a limit on how often one record can re-alert.
actual: sendImmediate for program A returns { sent: 0, capped: 1 }; no email goes out until the next digest (up to 24 h). The 60 emails all went to the attacker's own address. Nothing tells program A's members or the system administrator that the cap was hit (the count exists only in the action's return value in the Convex log).
evidence: repro/sec/zz-hunt-sec-emailcap.test.ts output: 'SE-3: { emailsToAttacker: 60, demoCheck: { capped: 1, sent: 0 ... }, toDemo: 0 }'. convex/urgentAlerts.ts:47-50 (one global key 'alerts:immediate'), :143-177 (claimDeliveries reserves one per recipient per check), src/domain/alerts.ts:516 (key includes the editable date); the same holds for inspection, AD and component keys, which include the editable due date (alerts.ts:265,317,374), so a maintenance member can do it by re-saving an overdue inspection (not run).
suspect: convex/urgentAlerts.ts:300 (reserveImmediateEmail: single deployment-wide key, no per-program or per-user share)

notes: Found while tracing what urgent emails can carry; not a security defect, but it is the most time-critical alert the feature exists for. The digest path predates 4 Nov (so digests have always missed report-only groundings); the urgent email and push paths are new. Correction to my first-round note: memberAlerts runs scopedSnapshot, which already applies the owner and board whitelists (src/domain/programs.ts:282-283), so once discrepancies are loaded a board member's email would carry 'Open discrepancy: ' with the description blanked, not the text. Check that wording when fixing. Round-two comparison of every alert kind against loadAlertSources: discrepancies are the only missing source (aircraftStatus and deferrals read s.discrepancies; dueItems reads aircraft, inspections, airworthiness, management, all loaded). title: An aircraft grounded by a pilot's grounding problem report (or an expired deferral) sends no urgent email, no push message and no digest line: the server's alert sources load no discrepancies, although the bell shows 'is grounded'.
steps: 1. Program with email (Resend) or push configured; an aircraft with nothing overdue. 2. A pilot files a problem report marked as grounding (status open, grounding true, no deferral). 3. operations.submit schedules urgentAlerts.sendImmediate ('New hours or a grounding report can make an alert urgent', convex/operations.ts:161). 4. Compare the bell in the app with the administrators' inboxes and devices.
expected: Opted-in members get '<program>: 1 urgent alert' with 'N206MA is grounded / Open discrepancy: ...' at once by email and on subscribed devices, and the daily digest lists it (docs/alerts.md line 18: the urgent check runs after 'a flight or problem report synced'; Settings text: 'Urgent alerts (a grounded aircraft, ...) open on this device as soon as they arise').
actual: In the app computeAlerts(snapshot) lists 'N206MA is grounded' with detail 'Open discrepancy: Nose gear strut flat. Do not fly.'. On the server sendImmediate returns { sent: 0, pushed: 0 } and sendDigests { sent: 0 }: no email at all. loadAlertSources builds the snapshot with discrepancies: [] ('members, flights, discrepancies and the change log stay empty, since no alert reads them'), but the aircraft-grounded alert is computed by aircraftStatus(), which reads s.discrepancies for grounding reports and for deferral expiry (src/domain/aircraftStatus.ts:241-265). So a grounding that comes only from a report or an expired MEL/deferral never leaves the app; when another reason also grounds the aircraft the email lists only the other reasons.
evidence: repro/sec/zz-hunt-sec-grounding-alert.test.ts output: 'SE-4: { inApp: [ "N206MA is grounded" ], urgent: { sent: 0, pushed: 0, ... }, digest: { sent: 0 }, emails: 0 }'. convex/alerts.ts:361-406 (loadAlertSources, discrepancies: [] at :402), src/domain/alerts.ts:466-489 (groundedAlerts via aircraftStatus), src/domain/aircraftStatus.ts:241-251. No test in convex/alerts.test.ts, urgentAlerts.test.ts or push.test.ts seeds a discrepancy.
